scope: Independent first-hand design evidence for Claude Desktop and app; historical brand provenance; no login/install/patching

sources.title: Geist: Anthropic case study
sources.author: Geist
sources.date: Undated; work spans prelaunch to mid-2023 Claude launch
sources.surface: Brand foundations and web/product component language
sources.confidence: high for historical intent; low for current app measurements
sources.finding: The original designers describe pairing Styrene with Tiempos, a warm color system, human-centered illustration, and function-led components across web and product. This establishes historical rationale, not October 2026 UI specifications.

sources.title: Work by Everett: Anthropic
sources.author: Everett Katigbak
sources.date: Portfolio labels role June 2023–Present; publication undated
sources.confidence: high for stated creative principles
sources.finding: The creative director says the brand deliberately favors warmth, accessibility, and restraint. His account attributes visual/art direction to Geist and Tim Belonax. It supports the emotional brief, not exact token values.

sources.title: Kyle Turman: Designing Claude and collaborating with AI
sources.author: Dive Club interview with Kyle Turman
sources.confidence: high for historical intent
sources.finding: Turman directly explains the warmer beige canvas and serif response text as decisions made with the brand team to make Claude feel human and suited to long reading. He also says many microdecisions were pragmatic and later refined; avoid inventing a grand rationale for every pixel.
sources.access: Original video transcript read with Exa; publisher episode page has no extractable body.

sources.title: Anthropic Brand Team Interview
sources.author: Carissa Justice interviewing Tim Belonax and Chelsea Larsson
sources.confidence: high for first-person principles
sources.finding: Belonax links the serif to bookish humanity, the sans to synthetic technology, and the palette to unfired clay. The team describes an unvarnished, collaborative voice that informs illustration and motion. Treat this as rationale, not proof of accessibility compliance.

sources.title: My Styrene Soul: A Short Affair with Claude.ai
sources.author: Andrew Boardman
sources.confidence: medium; historical visual inspection
sources.finding: Boardman observes a warm beige frame, rounded composer, soft shadow and quiet gray controls; he would separate controls more. His font identification names Galaxie Copernicus, Styrene B and Tiempos Text. Useful historical evidence of perceived calm; the names and estimated dimensions must not become current specifications.

sources.title: Claude Design System: repository and provenance
sources.author: 5j54d93
sources.confidence: medium for measured snapshots, not official
sources.finding: This project explicitly separates app and marketing tokens and provides raw archives, themed samples and implementation documentation. Its MIT notice covers documentation/CSS but excludes Anthropic logos, wordmark and fonts. A useful reference, not an official or current Anthropic design-system release.

sources.title: Claude Design System: June color capture
sources.author: 5j54d93
sources.date: Repository folder labels capture 2026-06; no day/build in payload
sources.confidence: medium-high for contents of capture; medium for production provenance
sources.finding: Parsed 317 color primitives plus light/dark semantic mappings. Light canvas resolves to #f8f8f6, elevated surface #ffffff, user-message surface #efeeeb; dark canvas #1f1f1e and raised surface #2c2c2a. Brand clay is #d97757. These are snapshot values, not October 2026 measurements.

sources.title: Claude Design System: color system
sources.author: 5j54d93
sources.confidence: medium
sources.finding: The author reports a shift from old ivory #faf9f5 to app #f8f8f6 and renames old orange/blue token families to brand-* and accent-*. The chapter explicitly preserves historical values. A document containing a hex does not establish that hex as the current app canvas.

sources.title: Claude Design System: typography
sources.author: 5j54d93
sources.confidence: medium; exact line-height unresolved
sources.finding: Reports Anthropic Sans for UI/user messages, Anthropic Serif for responses, and Anthropic Mono replacing earlier JetBrains Mono. Dark-mode weights are lighter, including bold 600→530. It warns the custom fonts are proprietary. Its response line-height claims conflict: 24px versus a 1.65rem class, so that measurement is unverified.

sources.title: Claude Design System: layout
sources.author: 5j54d93
sources.surface: App, with separately marked marketing section
sources.confidence: medium
sources.finding: Documents a 4px spacing base with 6px and 8px gaps, plus separate z-index roles for headers, sidebar, modal, popovers and toast. App fixed-rem rules and marketing fluid grids are distinct. Avoid importing marketing section padding or hero sizes into a desktop workbench.

sources.title: Claude Design System: components
sources.author: 5j54d93
sources.confidence: medium; not independently live-measured
sources.finding: Reports 288px sidebar, 20px composer radius, 12px user-message radius with 10×16px padding, 32px icon controls and 12px menu radius. Composer uses a faint ring plus soft shadow; responses are unboxed. Buttons include hover, pressed, focus and disabled states. These are attributed starting points, not a current desktop pixel-perfect specification.

sources.title: Claude Design System: shape and elevation
sources.author: 5j54d93
sources.confidence: medium
sources.finding: The component language uses graded radii and very faint boundaries. Menu elevation combines a 1px ring with two soft shadows; composer uses a half-pixel ring and much lighter shadow. The chapter distinguishes normal surfaces from floating overlays. Its catalog mixes dates and contexts, so select by component rather than applying one global radius.

sources.title: Claude Design System: motion
sources.author: 5j54d93
sources.confidence: medium
sources.finding: Documents short interaction durations, a 0.985 pressed scale, fade/zoom popovers, and shimmer/pulse loading feedback. Marketing motion uses a different stack. Claims of universal reduced-motion coverage were not independently tested. Use the quiet motion vocabulary but provide a real reduced-motion implementation in original code.

sources.title: Claude Design System: design playbook
sources.author: 5j54d93
sources.confidence: high as author's advice; low as official claim
sources.finding: Recommends choosing the surface and task density before components, using one primary action, restrained layering, and a complete default/hover/pressed/focus/disabled/loading/empty/error state matrix. Useful implementation methodology, but its inferred rules must be labeled as recommendations rather than Anthropic requirements.

sources.title: Claude Desktop theming token map
sources.author: patrickjaja
sources.confidence: medium-high with explicit provenance; internal contradictions noted
sources.finding: Documents coexisting legacy, v2 semantic, CDS and desktop-frame layers. Desktop frame uses df-* rather than chat bg-* tokens. Records 288px sidebar, 48px header and 26px rows. September additions describe CDS-backed pills, chips and row states. Several v1/v2-equality statements contradict its own numeric tables; use scoped resolved values, never merge them blindly.

sources.title: Claude Desktop Extra themes reference
sources.author: patrickjaja
sources.date: Reference corrected for v1.15962; current branch accessed 2026-10-14
sources.confidence: high for its own implementation; medium for upstream behavior
sources.finding: Explains why text, borders, filled-control text, CDS and frame surfaces need coordinated theme mapping. Low-alpha borders need a contrasting base token; pastel fills may need dark text. Its contrast claims apply to its custom themes, not an audit of stock Claude. No theme software was installed.

sources.title: Claude Desktop Bin custom themes
sources.author: vinnymeller
sources.confidence: medium
sources.finding: Separates main claude.ai conversation content from local Quick Entry, search and About windows, and documents HSL semantic versus legacy hex chrome variables. This supports testing multiple desktop windows instead of assuming one chat stylesheet covers every surface. Its theme-modification instructions are research only here.

sources.title: Claude Desktop Skin
sources.author: mohannad789
sources.confidence: high for author's own changes
sources.finding: The author deliberately adds a two-column sidebar, project colors/tags and a wider chat to reduce wasted space. This is useful counter-evidence to assuming Claude's density suits every work pattern. Its dimensions and visuals are modifications, not stock reference material; nothing was run.

sources.title: Claude AI Clone engineering showcase
sources.author: JonniTech
sources.confidence: high for stated project choices; low for fidelity
sources.finding: The author calls it pixel-perfect but states it uses Inter and #F4F3EE, which diverge from the measured snapshot's custom families and #f8f8f6. Keep as a reconstruction example; exclude from official typography, exact palette and security claims. No install, login or API-key entry was performed.

sources.title: Claude on Claude: a Design Study
sources.author: Michael Higgins
sources.confidence: high for concept; excluded as stock evidence
sources.finding: An explicitly reimagined interface uses blue/sage, Inter, GT Alpina and JetBrains Mono plus new motion. It is valuable as a contrasting interpretation. Its precise colors and timing are proposed design decisions, not evidence of Claude's shipped interface.

sources.title: Dark-blue-on-black desktop readability report
sources.author: mcbain and first-hand commenters
sources.kind: Primary issue report and user observations
sources.confidence: medium for historical regression; current status unverified
sources.finding: Users reported low-contrast Code messages and a mismatch with Chat/Cowork. A May 7 comment reported partial improvement; closure was inactivity-based, with a June 5 report that the problem remained. Neither closure nor complaint proves October 2026 state. Use as a regression-test warning.

sources.title: Windows RTL/font rendering report
sources.author: omidazg
sources.surface: Windows ARM64 Claude Desktop Code renderer
sources.confidence: medium-high for reported environment; not independently reproduced
sources.finding: The reporter provides rendered-width tests and bundle inspection for script fallback and mixed-direction failures. Closed as duplicate, not demonstrated fixed. Reusable UI should test Arabic/Persian/Hebrew mixed with Latin code and numbers, logical alignment, correct font fallback and per-block text direction.

sources.title: RTL text direction support tracker
sources.author: eitan-kir and first-hand commenters
sources.confidence: medium for lived experience; no app-wide audit
sources.finding: Desktop users describe mixed Hebrew/English ordering failures. October 9's terminal-plugin author explicitly says the workaround does not cover Desktop or the VS Code panel. Keep renderer distinctions: a terminal workaround is not evidence that desktop text rendering is fixed.

sources.title: Design Critique: Claude Mobile App
sources.author: Kali Birdsall
sources.confidence: medium for mobile observations; no desktop measurement
sources.finding: Observes a hierarchy from orange mark to greeting to input, with grouped communication controls. Critiques ambiguous microphone/waveform and model-choice signifiers. Useful cross-surface lesson: visual quiet needs accessible names and explanations; do not use the mobile layout as a desktop sizing source.

token_provenance: I07; HSL-to-sRGB HEX conversions computed here, rounded to 8-bit. Snapshot only, no original fonts/logos/code redistributed.

No October 2026 authoritative full state/token matrix.
Exact response line-height unresolved in I09.
